title: Equivariance of the twisted pairing
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect. With $F_{c,K}$ and $F_{K^\vee (d)}$ the operators of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] formed from $\varphi _K$ and the datum $\varphi _{K^\vee (d)}$ of [def-pod-dual-tate-datum], the degreewise pairings satisfy

$$
\bigl\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee (d)}y\bigr\rangle _i =\langle x,y\rangle _i \qquad \bigl(x\in H_c^i(X,K),\  y\in H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))\bigr),
$$

where the action on the second factor includes the scalar $q^{-d}$ on $A_X(d)$ and the pairing is the derived Poincare pairing in the form of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing].

proof.text: Work at the coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and with $a_X:X\to s$ of [def-pod-conventions]. Put $L=K^\vee(d)$, $W=A_X(d)$, $T=Lg^*$, and write $\phi=\varphi_K$, $\psi=\varphi_L$ and $t=\tau_d$. Both $K$ and $L$ are strict Weil complexes by [prop-pod-dual-tate-data-compatibility]. Let $e:K\otimes^L L\to W$ be the twisted evaluation in [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing]. Write $b:T(K\otimes^L L)\simeq TK\otimes^L TL$ for the tensor comparison and $v=(\phi\otimes\psi)b$. The untwisted evaluation equality in [prop-pod-dual-tate-data-compatibility] is $\operatorname{ev}(\phi\otimes\varphi_{K^\vee})b=t_0T(\operatorname{ev})$, with $t_0$ the canonical coefficient datum. Tensor this equality with $t$ and use $\psi=\varphi_{K^\vee}\otimes t$ from [def-pod-dual-tate-datum]. Since $e=\operatorname{ev}\otimes1_W$ through associativity and the coefficient-unit identification, this gives $ev=tT(e)$. The Tate datum has the required scalar $q^{-d}$; $q$ is invertible because $\ell\ne p$.

source.place: Step 1: equivariance of the twisted evaluation

proof.text:
Let $C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ and $D=R\Gamma(X,L)$, and put $F_C=R\Gamma_c(\phi)\tau_{c,K}$ and $F_D=R\Gamma(\psi)\tau_L$, as prescribed in [def-pod-conventions] (for $F_C$ this is clause 1 of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] at $m=1$). Set $F_{K\otimes L}=R\Gamma_c(v)\tau_{c,K\otimes L}$. The transport identity of [lem-pod-frobenius-cup-transport], followed by $R\Gamma_c(\phi\otimes\psi)$, gives
$$F_{K\otimes L}\mu_{K,L}=R\Gamma_c(\phi\otimes\psi)\mu_{TK,TL}(\tau_{c,K}\otimes\tau_L)=\mu_{K,L}(F_C\otimes F_D).$$
The second equality is precisely naturality in the two inputs of [prop-pod-cup-product-coherence]. Use the shifted identity of the transport lemma to read the same equation with the second input shifted by $[2d]$.

source.place: Steps 1-2: cup-product square for the induced cohomology operators

proof.text:
Set $F_W=R\Gamma_c(t)\tau_{c,W}$. Naturality of compact-support transport, explicitly stated in [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport], and the equality $ev=tT(e)$ from Step 1 give
$$R\Gamma_c(e)F_{K\otimes L}=R\Gamma_c(e v)\tau_{c,K\otimes L}=R\Gamma_c(t)R\Gamma_c(T(e))\tau_{c,K\otimes L}=F_WR\Gamma_c(e).$$
Shift this identity by $[2d]$, using the shift compatibility of [lem-pod-frobenius-cup-transport]. Let $P=R\Gamma_c(e)[2d]\circ\mu_{K,L[2d]}$ with the canonical tensor/shift comparisons. Combining with Step 2 gives $P(F_C\otimes F_D[2d])=F_W[2d]P$.

source.place: Step 2: compose cup product and evaluation

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] to $f=a_X$ and the constant coefficient object $A_s$ with its canonical datum. The hypotheses hold: $a_X$ is smooth separated of finite type of pure dimension $d$, and the same Tate datum $t$ is used in its purity source. The theorem's trace square is an equality $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}\circ\varphi_{a_!W[2d]}=\varphi_A\circ Lg_s^*(\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}})$ on $s$. Apply the point functor and precompose with point transport. Its naturality in [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] gives
$$\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}F_W[2d]=F_A\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}.$$
Here $F_A$ is point transport followed by the canonical datum. Its cohomology in degree zero is the identity by [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar] at $m=0$. By [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing], $\beta_K=\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}P$. Consequently Steps 2-3 give $\beta_K(F_C\otimes F_D[2d])=F_A\beta_K$.

source.place: Steps 1-2: the trace square and composition

proof.text:
For $x\in H^i(C)$ and $y\in H^{2d-i}(D)$, view $y$ as an element of $H^{-i}(D[2d])$. Their tensor class has degree zero. Applying degree-zero cohomology to the equality of Step 4 and evaluating on this tensor class yields
$$\langle H^i(F_C)x,H^{2d-i}(F_D)y\rangle_i=H^0(F_A)\langle x,y\rangle_i=\langle x,y\rangle_i.$$
The pairing is exactly the degreewise form specified by [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing], and the operators are $F_{c,K}$ and $F_{K^\vee(d)}$ by Step 2. The shift identity is $H^{-i}(D[2d])=H^{2d-i}(D)$; there is no interchange of inputs and hence no extra Koszul sign. By [def-pod-dual-tate-datum], the second operator uses $\varphi_{K^\vee}\otimes\tau_d$, including $q^{-d}$, as required.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1-3, with finite-coefficient cup transport exposed as a separate lemma

blueprint_update.statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect. With $F_{c,K}$ and $F_{K^\vee (d)}$ the operators of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] formed from $\varphi _K$ and the datum $\varphi _{K^\vee (d)}$ of [def-pod-dual-tate-datum], the degreewise pairings satisfy

$$
\bigl\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee (d)}y\bigr\rangle _i =\langle x,y\rangle _i \qquad \bigl(x\in H_c^i(X,K),\  y\in H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))\bigr),
$$

where the action on the second factor includes the scalar $q^{-d}$ on $A_X(d)$ and the pairing is the derived Poincare pairing in the form of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing].

proof.text:
Step 1: the derived pairing $\beta _K$ of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] is the composite of the mixed-support cup product, the evaluation, and the smooth trace. The mixed-support cup product is induced by the tensor product of sheaves and its $\Gamma _c$-realization, both equivariantly lifted to Weil complexes by [lem-fix-weil-operations], and the same statement applies to the global-sections functors $R\Gamma _c$ and $R\Gamma$ with the data of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]. The evaluation is a morphism of Weil objects by [prop-pod-dual-tate-data-compatibility]. The trace $\operatorname {Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,A}$ is equivariant by the trace square of [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace], whose source datum carries the twist normalization of the Tate line, [def-pur-tate-datum], and the target datum on $A$ is the canonical datum of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Step 2: composing, the tuple

$$
\bigl(R\Gamma _c(X,K),\  R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d],\  A\bigr)
$$

carries the Weil data $\varphi _{c,K},\  \varphi _{K^\vee (d)}$, and the canonical datum, and the pairing $\beta _K$ is a morphism of Weil objects from the tensor of the first two to the last, by Step 1 and the compatibility of the tensor product with the data in [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Step 3: on cohomology, in the degree-zero part

$$
\beta _K:\  H_c^i(X,K)\otimes H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)\to A
$$

of the pairing (the form of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing]), the induced operators are the $F$'s of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]: the operator on the first factor is $F_{c,K}$, and the operator on the second factor is $F_{K^\vee (d)}$, the datum $\varphi _{K^\vee (d)}$ containing the scalar $q^{-d}$ on $A_X(d)$ by [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] and [def-pur-tate-datum]. The morphism property of Step 2 evaluated on the tensor of two vectors gives

$$
\bigl\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee (d)}y\bigr\rangle _i =F\bigl(\langle x,y\rangle _i\bigr)
$$

with $F$ the global geometric Frobenius of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]; but the target datum is the canonical one, so $F$ acts on $A$ as the identity, by [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], giving the displayed identity.
